paragraphs: Saul Centers, Inc. ("Saul Centers") was incorporated under the Maryland General Corporation Law in 1993, and operates as a REIT under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"). The Company is required to annually distribute at least 90% of its REIT taxable income (excluding net capital gains) to its stockholders and meet certain organizational and other requirements. Saul Centers has made and intends to continue to make regular quarterly distributions to its stockholders. Saul Centers, together with its wholly-owned subsidiaries and the limited partnerships of which Saul Centers or one of its subsidiaries is the sole general partner, are referred to collectively as the "Company." B. Francis Saul II serves as Chairman of the Board of Directors (the "Board") and Chief Executive Officer of Saul Centers.

The Company's primary strategy is to continue to focus on diversification of its assets through development of transit-oriented, residential mixed-use projects and expansion of and additions to its grocery-anchored shopping centers in the Washington, DC/Baltimore metropolitan area. The Company's operating strategy also includes improvement of the operating performance of its assets, internal growth of its Shopping Centers through the addition of pad sites, and supplementing its development pipeline with selective redevelopment and renovations of its core Shopping Centers.

Saul Centers was formed to continue and expand the shopping center business previously owned and conducted by the B. F. Saul Real Estate Investment Trust (the "Saul Trust"), the B. F. Saul Company and certain other affiliated entities, each of which is controlled by B. Francis Saul II and his family members (collectively, the "Saul Organization"). In 1993, in connection with this restructuring, members of the Saul Organization transferred to Saul Holdings Limited Partnership, a newly formed Maryland limited partnership (the "Operating Partnership"), and two newly formed subsidiary limited partnerships (the "Subsidiary Partnerships," and collectively with the Operating Partnership, the "Partnerships"), certain shopping center and mixed-use properties, and the management functions related to the transferred properties. Since its formation, the Company has developed and purchased additional properties. The Company conducts its business through the Operating Partnership and/or directly or indirectly owned subsidiaries.

As of December 31, 2025, the Company's properties (the "Current Portfolio Properties") consisted of 50 shopping center properties (the "Shopping Centers"), nine mixed-use properties, which are comprised of office, retail and multi-family residential uses (the "Mixed-Use Properties") and three (non-operating) development properties.
Management of the Current Portfolio Properties

The Operating Partnership manages the Current Portfolio Properties and will manage any subsequently acquired or developed properties. The management of the properties includes performing property management, leasing, design, renovation, development and accounting duties for each property. The Operating Partnership provides each property with a fully integrated property management capability, with approximately 70 full-time equivalent employees at its headquarters office and 86 full-time employees and 12 part-time employees at its properties and with an extensive network of relationships with tenants and potential tenants as well as with members of the brokerage and property owners' communities. The Company currently does not, and does not intend to, retain third-party managers or provide management services to third parties.

The Company augments its property management capabilities by sharing with the Saul Organization certain ancillary functions, at cost, such as information technology, payroll services, human resources and benefits administration, accounting services, and in-house legal services. The Company also shares certain insurance administration expenses on a pro rata basis with the Saul Organization. Management believes that these arrangements result in lower costs than could be obtained by contracting with third parties. These arrangements permit the Company to capture greater economies of scale in purchasing from third-party vendors than would otherwise be available to the Company alone and to capture internal economies of scale by avoiding payments representing profits with respect to functions provided internally. The terms of all sharing arrangements with the Saul Organization, including payments related thereto, are specified in a written agreement and are reviewed periodically by the Audit Committee of the Company's Board of Directors.

The Company subleases its corporate headquarters space from the Saul Organization. A discussion of the lease terms is provided in Note 7, Long Term Lease Obligations, of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.

The principal offices of the Company are located at 7501 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 1500E, Bethesda, Maryland 20814-6522, and the Company's telephone number is (301) 986-6200. The Company's internet web address is www.saulcenters.com. Information contained on the Company's website is not part of this report. The Company makes available free of charge on its website its annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and any amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act, as soon as reasonably practicable after the reports are electronically filed with, or furnished to, the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). We intend to comply with the requirements of Item 5.05 of Form 8-K regarding amendments to and waivers under the code of business conduct and ethics applicable to our Chief Executive Officer, Principal Financial Officer and Principal Accounting Officer by providing such information on our website within four days after effecting any amendment to, or granting any waiver under, that code, and we will maintain such information on our website for at least twelve months. Alternatively, you may access these reports at the SEC's website: www.sec.gov.
Policies with Respect to Certain Activities

The following is a discussion of the Company's operating strategy and certain of its investment, financing and other policies. These strategies and policies have been determined by the Board of Directors and, in general, may be amended or revised from time to time by the Board of Directors without a vote of the Company's stockholders.

The Company's primary strategy is to continue to diversify its assets through development of transit-oriented, residential mixed-use projects and expansion of and additions to its grocery-anchored Shopping Centers in the Washington, DC/Baltimore metropolitan area. The Company's operating strategy also includes improvement of the operating performance of its assets, internal growth of its Shopping Centers through the addition of pad sites, and supplementing its development pipeline with selective redevelopment and renovations of its core Shopping Centers. The Company has a pipeline of entitled sites in its portfolio, some of which are currently Shopping Centers, for development of up to 2,500 apartment units and 850,000 square feet of retail and office space. All such sites are located proximate to Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority red line Metro stations in Montgomery County, Maryland. In addition, the Company recently entered into a lease with Publix to develop a new grocery store at Ashland Square in Prince William County, Virginia. When complete, Ashland Square is expected to ultimately comprise approximately 124,000 square feet of retail space including the 50,325 square foot Publix, three existing pad sites, four additional pad sites and approximately 30,000 square feet of small shop space.

Management believes there is potential for long term growth in cash flow as existing leases for space in the Shopping Centers and Mixed-Use Properties expire and are renewed, or newly available or vacant space is leased. Through its leasing activities, the Company intends to optimize the mix of uses at the Shopping Centers to improve foot traffic. Management's leasing goals are to increase occupancy, improve overall retail sales, and ultimately increase cash flow. In those circumstances in which leases are not otherwise expiring, management selectively attempts to increase cash flow through a variety of means, or in connection with renovations or relocations, recapturing leases with below market rents and re-leasing at market rates, as well as replacing financially troubled tenants. When possible, management also will seek to include scheduled increases in base rent, as well as percentage rent based on sales provisions, in its leases.

It is management's intention to hold properties for long-term investment and management places strong emphasis on regular maintenance, periodic renovation and capital improvement. Management believes that characteristics such as cleanliness, lighting and security are particularly important in community and neighborhood shopping centers, which are frequently visited by shoppers during hours outside of the normal workday. Management believes that the Shopping Centers and Mixed-Use Properties generally are attractive and well maintained. The Shopping Centers and Mixed-Use Properties will undergo expansion, renovation, reconfiguration and modernization from time to time when management believes that such action is warranted by opportunities or changes in the competitive environment of a property. The Company will continue its practice of expanding existing properties by undertaking new construction on outparcels suitable for development as free-standing retail or office facilities.

headings: Risk Factors Related to our Real Estate Investments and Operations
Revenue from our properties may be negatively impacted if the operations of our retail tenants are not successful.
We may be unable to collect balances due from tenants that file for bankruptcy protection.
Our ability to increase our net income depends on the success and continued presence of our shopping center "anchor" tenants and other significant tenants.
We may experience difficulty or delay in renewing leases or leasing vacant space.
Our development activities are inherently risky.
Redevelopments and acquisitions may fail to perform as expected.
Our performance and value are subject to general risks associated with the real estate industry.
Geographic concentration of our portfolio may make us particularly susceptible to adverse economic developments in the real estate markets of those areas.
Our results of operations may be negatively affected by adverse trends in the retail, office and residential real estate sectors.
The short-term nature of apartment leases exposes us more quickly to the effects of declining market rents, potentially making our results of operations and cash flows more volatile.
Many real estate costs are fixed, even if income from our properties decreases.
Competition may limit our ability to purchase new properties and generate sufficient income from tenants.
The continued shift in retail sales towards e-commerce may adversely affect our financial condition, cash flows, and results of operations.
AI presents risks and challenges that could adversely affect our business, results of operations and reputations.
Cybersecurity risks and cyber incidents could adversely affect our business, disrupt operations and expose us to liabilities to tenants, employees, capital providers and other third parties.
We may be unable to sell properties when appropriate because real estate investments are illiquid.
Our real estate assets may become impaired.
Risk Factors Related to our Funding Strategies and Capital Structure
We have substantial relationships with members of the Saul Organization whose interests could conflict with the interests of other stockholders.
The amount of debt we have and the restrictions imposed by that debt could adversely affect our business and financial condition.

We are obligated to comply with financial and other covenants in our debt that could restrict our operating activities, and the failure to comply could result in defaults that accelerate the payment under our debt.
The market value of our debt and equity securities is subject to various factors that may cause significant fluctuations or volatility.
Our ability to grow will be limited if we cannot obtain additional capital.
Risk Factors Related to our REIT Status and Other Laws and Regulations
Environmental laws and regulations could reduce the value or profitability of our properties.
The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (the "ADA") or similar current or future legislation could require us to take remedial steps with respect to our properties.
The revenue generated by our tenants could be negatively affected by various federal, state and local laws to which they are subject.
We could be subject to legal or regulatory proceedings that may adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Failure to qualify as a REIT for federal income tax purposes would cause us to be taxed as a corporation, which would substantially reduce funds available for payment of distributions.
We may be required to incur additional debt to qualify as a REIT.
Legislative, administrative, regulatory or other actions affecting REITs, including positions taken by the IRS, could have a material adverse effect on us and our investors.
To maintain our status as a REIT, we limit the amount of shares any one stockholder can own.
General Risk Factors
Financial and economic conditions may have an adverse impact on us, our tenants' businesses and our results of operations.
Loss of our key management could adversely affect performance and the value of our common shares.
paragraphs: Carefully consider the following risks and all of the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto. If any of the events or developments described below were actually to occur, the Company's business, financial condition or results of operations could be adversely affected. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
In this section, unless the context indicates otherwise, the terms "Company," "we," "us" and "our" refer to Saul Centers, Inc., and its subsidiaries, including the Operating Partnership.

Adverse changes in consumer spending or consumer preferences for particular goods, services or store-based retailing could negatively impact the ability of our retail tenants to pay rent. Revenue from our properties depends primarily on the ability of our retail tenants to pay the full amount of rent due under their leases on a timely basis, which is in turn dependent on the success of their operations, making us vulnerable to general economic downturns and other conditions affecting the retail industry. Some of our leases provide for the payment of additional rent above the base amount based on a specified percentage of the gross sales generated by the retail tenants. As a result, declines in our retail tenants' sales revenue could adversely impact the Company's receipt of percentage rents required to be paid by tenants under certain leases. Some retail tenants may terminate their leases or vacate space due to an inability to operate profitably for an extended period of time, impacting the Company's ability to maintain occupancy levels.

Any reduction in the ability of our retail tenants, particularly our anchor tenants, to pay base rent or percentage rent may have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations. Small business retail tenants and anchor retailers that lease space in the Company's properties may experience a deterioration in their sales or other revenue, or a constraint on the availability of credit necessary to fund operations, which in turn may adversely impact those tenants' ability to pay contractual base rents and operating expense recoveries.

Historically and from time to time, certain of our tenants have experienced financial difficulties and filed for bankruptcy protection, typically under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code. If a tenant or lease guarantor files for bankruptcy, we may not be able to collect all pre-petition amounts owed by that party. In addition, a tenant that files for bankruptcy protection may reject or terminate our lease, in which event we would have a general unsecured claim that would likely be for less than the full amount owed to us for the remainder of the lease term, which could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. In the event that a tenant with a significant number of leases in our shopping centers files for bankruptcy protection and rejects its leases, we may experience a significant reduction in our revenues and may not be able to collect all pre-petition amounts owed by such tenant.

A majority of our shopping center properties are anchored by one or more major tenants, most of whom primarily offer day-to-day necessities and services. Thirty-four of our properties are anchored by a grocery store. Our net income could be adversely affected in the event of a downturn in the business, or the bankruptcy or insolvency, of any anchor store or anchor tenant. Our largest shopping center anchor tenant by revenue is Giant Food, which accounted for 4.5% of our total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025. The closing of one or more anchor stores prior to the expiration of the applicable lease term, or the termination of a lease by one or more of a property's anchor tenants could adversely affect that property and result in lease terminations by, or reductions in rent from, other tenants whose leases may permit termination or rent reduction in those circumstances or whose own operations may suffer as a result. In the event that we are unable to re-lease space vacated by an anchor tenant, we may incur additional expenses to reconfigure or re-model the space to be able to re-lease the space to one or more new anchor tenants or other tenants. This could reduce our net income and negatively impact our financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and related footnotes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We make statements in this section that are forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. For a complete discussion of forward-looking statements, see the section in this report entitled "Forward-Looking Statements." Certain risks may cause our actual results, performance or achievements to differ materially from those expressed or implied by the following discussion. For a discussion of such risk factors, see "Item 1A. Risk Factors."

The Company's primary strategy is to continue to diversify its assets through development of transit-oriented, residential mixed-use projects and expansion of and additions to its grocery-anchored Shopping Centers in the Washington, DC/Baltimore metropolitan area. The Company's operating strategy also includes improvement of the operating performance of its assets, internal growth of its Shopping Centers through the addition of pad sites, and supplementing its development pipeline with selective redevelopment and renovations of its core Shopping Centers. The Company has a pipeline of entitled sites in its portfolio, some of which are currently Shopping Centers, for development of up to 2,500 apartment units and 850,000 square feet of retail and office space. All such sites are located proximate to Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority red line Metro stations in Montgomery County, Maryland. In addition, the Company recently entered into a lease with Publix to develop a new grocery store at Ashland Square in Prince William County, Virginia. When complete, Ashland Square is expected to ultimately comprise approximately 124,000 square feet of retail space including the 50,325 square foot Publix, three existing pad sites, four additional pad sites and approximately 30,000 square feet of small shop space.

The Company intends to selectively add free-standing pad site buildings within its Shopping Center portfolio and replace underperforming tenants with tenants that generate strong traffic, including anchor stores such as grocery stores. The Company has two executed leases and six leases are under negotiation for a total of eight more pad sites.

In recent years, there has been a limited amount of quality properties for sale. Management believes it will continue to be challenging to identify acquisition opportunities for investment in existing and new shopping center and mixed-use properties into the near future. It is management's view that several of the sub-markets in which the Company operates have, or are expected to have in the future, attractive supply/demand characteristics. The Company will continue to evaluate acquisition, development and redevelopment as integral parts of its overall business plan.

Actions taken by the Federal government will likely continue to impact the office, retail and residential real estate markets in the Washington, DC/Baltimore metropolitan area over the coming years. Because the majority of the Company's property net operating income is produced by our Shopping Centers, we continually monitor the implications of government policy changes, as well as shifts in consumer demand between on-line and in-store shopping, on future shopping center construction and retailer store expansion and closure plans. Based on our observations, we continue to adapt our marketing and merchandising strategies in ways to maximize our future performance. The Company's commercial leasing percentage, on a same property basis, which excludes the impact of properties not in operation for the entirety of the comparable periods, decreased to 94.6% at December 31, 2025, from 95.2% at December 31, 2024.

The Company maintains a ratio of total debt to total asset value of under 50%, which allows us to obtain additional secured borrowings if necessary. As of December 31, 2025, including $100.0 million of hedged variable-rate debt, total fixed-rate debt with staggered maturities from 2026 to 2041 represented approximately 88.4% of the Company's notes payable, thus minimizing refinancing risk. The Company's unhedged variable-rate debt consists of $189.0 million outstanding under the New Credit Facility. As of December 31, 2025, the Company has availability of approximately $96.2 million under its New Credit Facility.

Although it is management's present intention to concentrate future acquisition and development activities on transit-oriented, residential mixed-use properties and grocery-anchored shopping centers in the Washington, DC/Baltimore metropolitan area, the Company may, in the future, also acquire other types of real estate in other areas of the country as opportunities present themselves. The Company plans to continue to diversify in terms of property types, locations, size and market, and it does not set any limit on the amount or percentage of assets that may be invested in any one property or any one geographic area.

The Company's consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States ("GAAP"), which requires management to make certain estimates and assumptions that affect the reporting of financial position and results of operations. See Note 2 to the Consolidated Financial Statements in this report. The Company has identified the following policies that, due to estimates and assumptions inherent in those policies, involve a relatively high degree of judgment and complexity.

Real estate investment properties are stated at historic cost less depreciation. Although the Company intends to own its real estate investment properties over a long term, from time to time it will evaluate its market position, market conditions, and other factors and may elect to sell properties that do not conform to the Company's investment profile. Management believes that the Company's real estate assets have generally appreciated in value since their acquisition or development and, accordingly, the aggregate current value exceeds their aggregate net book value and also exceeds the value of the Company's liabilities as reported in the financial statements. Because the financial statements are prepared in conformity with GAAP, they do not report the current value of the Company's real estate investment properties.

If there is an event or change in circumstance that indicates a potential impairment in the value of a real estate investment property, the Company prepares an analysis to determine whether the carrying amount of the real estate investment property exceeds its estimated fair value. The Company considers both quantitative and qualitative factors when identifying impairment indicators including recurring operating losses, significant decreases in occupancy, and significant adverse changes in market conditions, legal factors and business climate. If impairment indicators are present, the Company compares the projected cash flows of the property over its remaining useful life, on an undiscounted basis, to the carrying amount of that property. The Company assesses its undiscounted projected cash flows based upon estimated capitalization rates, historic operating results and market conditions that may affect the property. If the carrying amount is greater than the undiscounted projected cash flows, the Company would recognize an impairment loss equivalent to an amount required to adjust the carrying amount to its then estimated fair value. The fair value of any property is sensitive to the actual results of any of the aforementioned estimated factors, either individually or taken as a whole. Should the actual results differ from management's projections, the valuation could be negatively or positively affected.
Accounts Receivable, Accrued Income, and Allowance for Doubtful Accounts

Accounts receivable are primarily comprised of rental and reimbursement billings due from tenants, and straight-line rent receivables representing the cumulative amount of adjustments necessary to present rental income on a straight-line basis. Individual leases are assessed for collectability and, upon the determination that the collection of rents is not probable, accrued rent and accounts receivable are charged off, and the charge off is reflected as an adjustment to rental revenue. Revenue from leases where collection is not probable is recorded on a cash basis until collectability is determined to be probable. We also assess whether operating lease receivables, at the portfolio level, are appropriately valued based upon an analysis of balances outstanding, effects of tenant bankruptcies, historical levels of bad debt and current economic trends. Evaluating and estimating uncollectable lease payments and related receivables requires a significant amount of judgment by management and is based on the best information available to management at the time of evaluation. Actual results could differ from these estimates.

The Company is subject to various legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of business, which are generally covered by insurance. While the resolution of these matters cannot be predicted with certainty, the Company believes the final outcome of current matters will not have a material adverse effect on its financial position or the results of operations. Upon determination that a loss is probable to occur, the estimated amount of the loss is recorded in the financial statements. Both the amount of the loss and the point at which its occurrence is considered probable can be difficult to determine.

Saul Centers, Inc. ("Saul Centers") 於 1993 年根據馬裏蘭州公司法設立，並根據 1986 年內政部稅法（the "Code"）作為 REIT 運作。本公司每年必須至少將其 REIT 稅收所得（扣除淨資本利得後）的 90% 分配給股東，並符合某些組織及其他要求。Saul Centers 已經並有意繼續定期向股東發放季度現金紅利。Saul Centers 連同其全資子公司及 Saul Centers 或其子公司為唯一普通合夥人的有限合夥企業， collectively 稱為 "本公司"。B. Francis Saul II 為董事會（the "Board"）主席及首席執行官（Chief Executive Officer）。
本公司主要策略為持續透過發展以交通為導向的住宅混合用途項目及擴充並增加其位於華盛頓特區/巴爾的摩都會區的超市為主的購物中心，來分散其資產。本公司運營策略亦包括改善其資產的運營表現、透過增加 pad sites 來實現購物中心的內在成長，並透過選擇性重新開發及翻修其核心購物中心來補充其開發管道。

Saul Centers 被設立以繼續並擴展先前由 B. F. Saul 房地產投資信託（the "Saul Trust"）、B. F. Saul 公司及其他相關實體所擁有並經營的購物中心業務，這些實體均由 B. Francis Saul II 及其家族成員控制（collectively，the "Saul Organization"）。1993 年，根據此重整，Saul Organization 的成員將其持有的購物中心及混合用途財產，以及與這些財產相關的管理功能，轉讓至 Saul Holdings Limited Partnership，一個新設立的馬裏蘭州有限合夥企業（the "Operating Partnership"），以及兩個新設立的子公司有限合夥企業（the "Subsidiary Partnerships"，與 Operating Partnership 合稱為 "Partnerships"）。自設立以來，本公司已開發並購入更多財產。本公司透過 Operating Partnership 及/或直接或間接擁有之子公司進行業務運作。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司財產（the "Current Portfolio Properties"）包含 50 個購物中心（the "Shopping Centers"）、九個混合用途財產，這些財產包含辦公室、零售及多戶住宅用途（the "Mixed-Use Properties"），以及三個（非運營）開發財產。
Current Portfolio Properties 管理

Operating Partnership 管理 Current Portfolio Properties，並會管理其後取得或開發的任何財產。財產管理包括執行財產管理、租賃、設計、翻修、開發及會計工作。Operating Partnership 為每個財產提供完整的整合式財產管理能力，其總部辦公室約有 70 名全職等效員工，其財產所在地有 86 名全職員工及 12 名兼職員工，並擁有廣泛的租客及潛在租客關係網路，以及與經紀公司及財產所有者社羣的關係。本公司目前並不會，也沒有意圖聘請第三方管理機構或向第三方提供管理服務。

本公司透過與 Saul Organization 共享某些輔助功能，以增強其財產管理能力，這些功能包括資訊科技、薪資服務、人力資源及福利管理、會計服務及內部法律服務，皆以成本為基礎進行。本公司亦與 Saul Organization 按比例分擔部分保險管理費用。管理層認為這些安排的總成本低於與第三方簽約的總成本。這些安排使本公司能從第三方供應商處獲得更大的規模經濟效益，並透過避免支付內部提供功能所代表的利潤，實現內部規模經濟效益。與 Saul Organization 的所有共享安排條款，包括相關付款，皆以書面協議明確規定，並由本公司董事會審計委員會定期審查。
本公司將其總部辦公室空間出租給 Saul Organization。有關租賃條款的討論請參見財務報表附註第 7 項，長期租賃義務附註。

關於特定活動之政策
以下為本公司營運策略及部分投資、融資及其他政策之說明。這些策略與政策已由董事會決定，通常可由董事會隨時修改或變更，無需經本公司股東投票通過。

本公司之主要策略為持續透過發展以捷運為導向之住宅混合用途項目，以及擴充及增加其位於華盛頓特區/巴爾的摩都會區之超市為主之購物中心，以分散其資產。本公司營運策略亦包括改善其資產之營運表現，透過增加附屬用地以實現購物中心之內在成長，並透過選擇性重新開發與翻新其核心購物中心，以補足其開發管道。本公司資產組閤中有一系列已取得開發許可之用地，其中部分目前為購物中心，用以開發最多 2,500 個公寓單位及 850,000 平方英呎之零售與辦公空間。所有這些用地均位於馬裏蘭州蒙哥馬利縣之華盛頓都會區捷運紅線地鐵站附近。此外，本公司最近與 Publix 簽訂租賃契約，以在維吉尼亞州阿什蘭德廣場開發一家新超市。完工後，阿什蘭德廣場預計將包含約 124,000 平方英呎之零售空間，包括 50,325 平方英呎之 Publix、三個現有附屬用地、四個新增附屬用地及約 30,000 平方英呎之小型商店空間。

管理層認為，現有購物中心與混合用途物業之租賃合約到期並續約，或新空置空間出租，將有潛在之長期現金流成長機會。透過其租賃活動，本公司意圖優化購物中心之使用組合，以提高人潮。管理層之租賃目標為提高佔用率、改善整體零售銷售額，並最終提高現金流。在租賃合約未到期之情況下，管理層會選擇性透過多種方式提高現金流，或在翻新或遷移時，重新出租原本以低於市場租金簽訂之租賃契約，並以市場租金重新出租，以及更換財務困難之租戶。在可行之情況下，管理層亦會在租賃契約中納入定期提高基本租金，以及根據銷售額之百分比租金條款。

管理層意圖長期持有不動產以進行投資，並強調定期維護、定期翻新與資本改善。管理層認為，清潔度、照明與安全等特性在社區與住宅購物中心尤其重要，因為這些購物中心常在正常工作時間之外被顧客造訪。管理層認為，購物中心與混合用途物業通常具有吸引力且維護良好。購物中心與混合用途物業將根據管理層認為有機會或競爭環境變化而進行擴張、翻新、重新配置與現代化。本公司將持續執行擴充現有不動產之慣例，透過在適合開發為獨立零售或辦公設施之附屬用地進行新興建設。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應與本年度10-K表報中所包含的合併財務報表及相關腳註一併閱讀。我們在本節中所提出的陳述屬於美國聯邦證券法規所定義的向前看聲明。有關向前看聲明的完整討論，請參閱本報告中標題為「向前看聲明」的節。某些風險可能導致本公司實際結果、表現或成就與以下討論所表達或暗示者有重大差異。有關這些風險因素的討論，請參閱「項目1A. 風險因素。」

本公司主要策略為透過發展以交通為導向的住宅混合用途項目，以及擴充並增加其位於華盛頓特區/巴爾的摩都會區的超市為主體的購物中心，來持續分散其資產。本公司營運策略亦包括改善其資產的營運表現，透過增加零組件來實現購物中心的內生成長，並透過選擇性重新開發與翻修其核心購物中心，來補足其開發管道。本公司在其資產組閤中擁有開發管道的已取得權限的零組件，其中一些目前為購物中心，用於開發最多2,500個公寓單位及850,000平方英呎的零售與辦公空間。所有這些零組件均位於馬裏蘭州蒙哥馬利縣華盛頓都會區紅線地鐵站附近。此外，本公司最近與Publix簽訂租賃契約，用於在維吉尼亞州阿什蘭德廣場開發新的超市。完工後，阿什蘭德廣場預期最終將包含約124,000平方英呎的零售空間，包括50,325平方英呎的Publix、三個現有零組件、四個額外零組件及約30,000平方英呎的小商店空間。
本公司有意選擇性地在其購物中心資產組閤中增加獨立零組件建築物，並以能產生強勁人潮的租戶取代表現不佳的租戶，包括超市等主要租戶。本公司已簽訂兩份租賃契約，並有六份租賃契約正在協商中，總計將增加八個零組件。
近年來，可供銷售的優質資產有限。管理層認為，在可預見的未來，尋找現有及新購物中心與混合用途資產的投資機會仍將具有挑戰性。管理層認為，本公司所經營的幾個次級市場，或預期未來將具有吸引人的供應與需求特徵。本公司將持續評估收購、開發與重新開發作為其整體業務計畫的重要組成部分。

美國聯邦政府所採取的行動，將可能在未來幾年持續影響華盛頓特區/巴爾的摩都會區的辦公、零售與住宅不動產市場。由於本公司絕大多數的財產淨營業收入來自於我們的購物中心，我們持續監測政府政策變動，以及消費者需求在線上與實體商店之間的轉變，對未來購物中心建設與零售商商店擴張與關閉計畫的影響。根據我們的觀察，我們持續調整我們的行銷與商品策略，以最大化我們未來的表現。本公司在相同財產基礎上，商業租賃比率（排除未在比較期間內全期營運的財產影響）於2025年12月31日降至94.6%，較2024年12月31日的95.2%為低。

本公司維持總負債對總資產價值比率低於50%，這使我們在必要時能夠取得額外的擔保貸款。截至2025年12月31日，包括100.0百萬美元的已套期保值變動利率負債，總固定利率負債（分階段到期日從2026年至2041年）約佔本公司應付票據的88.4%，從而降低再融資風險。本公司未套期保值的變動利率負債為根據新信貸協議下189.0百萬美元的現有負債。截至2025年12月31日，本公司根據新信貸協議下擁有約96.2百萬美元的信貸額度。
雖然管理層目前的意圖是將未來的收購與開發活動集中於華盛頓特區/巴爾的摩都會區的以交通為導向的住宅混合用途資產與超市為主體的購物中心，但本公司未來也可能根據機會取得美國其他地區的其他類型不動產。本公司計畫持續在資產類型、地點、規模與市場方面進行多元化，且本公司對任何單一資產或任何單一地理區域的投資金額或比例不設限。
本公司合併財務報表係根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）編製，這要求管理層做出某些會影響財務狀況與營運結果報告的估計與假設。請參閱本報告中合併財務報表的附註2。本公司已識別出以下政策，由於這些政策內固有的估計與假設，涉及相當高的判斷與複雜性。
不動產投資物業以歷史成本減折舊計價。雖然本公司有意長期持有其不動產投資物業，但有時會評估其市場地位、市場條件及其他因素，並可能選擇出售不符合本公司投資策略的物業。管理層認為，本公司不動產資產自取得或開發以來價值通常有所增加，因此，其當前價值總額超過其帳面淨值總額，同時也超過本公司在財務報表中報告的負債價值。由於財務報表係依照GAAP編製，因此未報導本公司不動產投資物業的當前價值。

若發生事件或情況變更，顯示不動產投資物業價值可能受損，本公司會進行分析以確定不動產投資物業的帳面價值是否高於其預估公平價值。本公司在識別價值受損跡象時，會考慮定量與定性因素，包括持續營運虧損、佔用率顯著下降，以及市場條件、法律因素及商業環境的重大不利變動。若存在價值受損跡象，本公司會將該物業在其剩餘使用壽命內的預測現金流（未貼現）與其帳面價值進行比較。本公司根據預估資本化率、歷史營運結果及可能影響該物業的市場條件，評估其未貼現預測現金流。若帳面價值高於未貼現預測現金流，本公司將認列價值受損損失，以調整帳面價值至當時預估公平價值。任何物業的公平價值對上述預估因素的實際結果敏感，無論是單獨或整體而言。若實際結果與管理層預測不同，估值可能受到負面或正面影響。
應收帳款、應計收入及應收帳款減損準備

應收帳款主要由租賃及補償發票應收自租戶，以及代表調整金額總計以呈現租金收入於直線基礎之應收租金組成。個別租賃會評估其可收回性，若確定租金無法收回，則應計租金及應收帳款會被核銷，並反映為租金收入的調整。對於租金無法收回的租賃，收入會以現金基礎記帳，直至確定租金可收回為止。我們也會評估於投資組合層面，經營租賃應收帳款是否適當計價，根據對未償還餘額、租戶破產影響、歷史壞帳水準及當前經濟趨勢的分析。評估及預估無法收回的租賃付款及相關應收帳款，需要管理層做出大量判斷，並基於評估時管理層可取得的最佳資訊。實際結果可能與這些預估不同。
本公司面臨各種法律程序及聲請，這些聲請通常係因業務運作而產生，並一般由保險覆蓋。雖然無法確定這些事項的解決結果，但本公司認為目前事項的最終結果不會對其財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。一旦確定損失將發生，則預估損失金額會計入財務報表中。損失金額及其發生時間點的判斷可能相當困難。
以下為本公司整體收入及費用組成的說明。本節一般討論2025年及2024年的項目，以及2025年與2024年之間的年度比較。未包含於本Form 10-K中的2023年項目及2024年與2023年之間的年度比較，可參閱我們於2024年12月31日財務年度結束後所提交的Form 10-K年度報告，於第二部分第7項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之分析」中。

headings: 風險因素與我們的不動產投資及營運相關
若我們的零售租戶營運不成功，我們的不動產收入可能會受到負面影響。
我們可能無法從申請破產保護的租戶收取應收帳款。
我們增加淨收入的能力取決於我們購物中心「主力租戶」及其他重要租戶的成功營運與持續在場。
我們可能在續約租賃或出租空置空間時遇到困難或延遲。
我們的開發活動本質上具有風險。
重新開發與收購可能無法如預期般表現。
我們的營運表現與價值受不動產業界一般風險影響。
本公司資產組成的地理集中性，可能使我們特別容易受到那些地區不動產市場不利經濟發展的影響。
本公司營運成果可能因零售、辦公室及住宅不動產產業的不利趨勢而受到負面影響。
公寓租賃的短期性使我們更快面臨市場租金下降的影響，可能使本公司營運成果及現金流更加波動。
許多不動產成本為固定成本，即使來自我們不動產的收入減少，這些成本仍會持續存在。
競爭可能限制我們購買新不動產及從租戶產生足夠收入的能力。
零售銷售持續向電子商務轉移，可能對本公司財務狀況、現金流及營運成果產生負面影響。
人工智能帶來的風險與挑戰，可能對本公司業務、營運成果及聲譽產生負面影響。
網路安全風險及網路事件可能對本公司業務造成影響，幹擾營運，並使本公司對租戶、員工、資金提供者及其他第三方承擔責任。
我們可能無法在適當的時機出售不動產，因為不動產投資屬流動性較差的資產。
我們的不動產資產可能發生減值。
與我們融資策略及資本結構相關的風險因素
我們與 Saul 組織成員擁有廣泛的關係，其利益可能與其他股東的利益產生衝突。
我們所負的債務金額及該債務所施加的限制條件，可能對我們的業務及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們有義務遵守債務中所規定的財務及其他契約條款，這些條款可能限制我們的營運活動，若未能遵守，可能導致違約，進而加速債務償還。
我們的債務及權益證券市場價值可能受到多種因素影響，這些因素可能導致顯著波動或不穩定。
若我們無法取得額外資金，將會限制我們的成長能力。
風險因素與我們的REIT地位及其他法律法規相關
環境法規可能降低我們不動產的價值或獲利能力。
1990年美國殘障法案（the "ADA"）或類似的現行或未來立法，可能要求我們針對不動產採取補救措施。
我們租戶所產生的收入可能因他們所受的聯邦、州及地方法律而受到負面影響。
我們可能面臨法律或監管程序，可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
若未能符合美國聯邦所得稅目的的REIT資格，將導致我們被課以公司稅，這將大幅減少用以支付股息的資金。
我們可能需要增加負債以符合REIT資格。
影響REIT的立法、行政、監管或其他行動，包括國稅局的立場，可能對我們及我們的投資人產生重大不利影響。
為維持本公司作為REIT之地位，我們限制任何一位股東所能擁有的股份數量。
一般風險因素
財務及經濟狀況可能對本公司、我們的租戶業務及我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
失去我們的關鍵管理層可能對績效及普通股之價值產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 請謹慎考量下列風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中所載的其他資訊，包括合併財務報表及其附註。若下列所描述的任何事件或發展實際發生，將可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成不利影響。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為我們所知或認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果。
在本節中，除非文意另有明確指示，否則「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」均指 Saul Centers, Inc. 及其子公司，包括營運合夥企業。

消費者支出減少或對特定商品、服務或商店零售的偏好改變，可能影響我們零售租戶支付租金的能力。我們財產的收入主要取決於零售租戶能否按時支付其租賃契約中應付的全部租金，而這又取決於其營運的成效，使我們面臨總體經濟衰退及其他影響零售業的條件。部分租賃契約規定，租戶需根據零售租戶產生的總銷售額的特定百分比，支付額外租金。因此，零售租戶銷售收入的下降，可能對本公司收取租戶根據某些租賃契約應支付的百分比租金造成不利影響。部分零售租戶可能因無法長時間營運獲利而終止租賃契約或搬離空間，影響本公司維持佔用率的能力。
我們零售租戶，特別是主要租戶，支付基本租金或百分比租金的能力下降，可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。租賃本公司財產空間的小型零售租戶及主要零售商，可能經歷銷售或其他收入的惡化，或信貸可用性的限制，以資助營運，這進而可能影響這些租戶支付合約基本租金及營運費用回收的能力。

歷史上及時而，部分租戶曾經驗到財務困難並申請破產保護，通常根據美國破產法。若租戶或租賃擔保人申請破產保護，我們可能無法收回該當事人應付的全部破產前金額。此外，申請破產保護的租戶可能拒絕或終止我們的租賃契約，若此情況發生，我們將擁有無擔保的一般索賠，該索賠很可能低於我們對租賃契約剩餘期間應收的全部金額，這可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。若某租戶在本公司購物中心擁有大量租賃契約，並申請破產保護並拒絕其租賃契約，我們可能經驗到收入的重大減少，且可能無法收回該租戶應付的全部破產前金額。

我們購物中心的大多數財產均由一個或多個主要租戶所支撐，這些主要租戶主要提供日常必需品及服務。我們有三十四處財產由一家超市所支撐。若任何主要租戶或主要租戶發生業務衰退，或破產或財務困難，將可能對我們的淨收入造成不利影響。我們最大的購物中心主要租戶（按收入計算）為 Giant Food，該租戶在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度中，佔我們總收入的4.5%。若某個主要租戶在租賃契約到期前關閉，或終止其租賃契約，將可能對該財產造成不利影響，並導致其他租戶終止租賃契約或減少租金，特別是那些租賃契約允許在這種情況下終止租賃或減少租金的租戶，或其自身營運因上述情況而受影響的租戶。若我們無法重新出租由主要租戶離開所空出的空間，我們可能需要增加費用以重新配置或重新裝潢空間，以便重新出租給一個或多個新主要租戶或其他租戶。這可能會減少我們的淨收入，並對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成負面影響。
